newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Autonomy for Brazil forensic teams urged.
newsitem.headline: Autonomy for Brazil forensic teams urged.

text.p: Amnesty International urged Brazil on Friday to make forensic pathologists independent of the police, whose members are suspected in Brazil's worst human rights crimes.
"Without this autonomy, it makes it very difficult to expose the truth about human rights violations," Alison Sutton, an analyst for the London-based human rights organisation, said.
"There's a great tendency on the part of the police to destroy or omit forensic evidence," she added.

At a press conference in Sao Paulo, Amnesty called for federal legislation to ensure the autonomy of forensic doctors, who are now subordinate to state public safety offices that oversee Brazil's police.

The group also asked Brazil's federal and state governments to ensure that detainees are given medical exams before being booked and after being released to ascertain if they have been tortured in custody.

Sutton cited recent controversies over forensic investigations in Brazil's most notorious human rights cases, including the April massacre of 19 landless peasants by military police in the state of Para.
She said impunity was one of Brazil's biggest human rights problems and called cases stalled by a lack of forensic evidence and the usual long delays in Brazil's courts "a time-bomb ticking away."
Autonomy for forensic pathologists is supported by Brazil's Society for Forensic Pathologists, which has lobbied for it since 1989, and fiercely opposed by the police, Sutton said.
